bull_bear.body:
- Single-product specialisation in centreless grinding machines serving multiple industrial end-markets (automobile, auto ancillary, textile machinery, steel, bearings)
- Established export presence to the U.S.A. and Europe, with new avenues opened to Australia, South America and South East Asia
- Ability to sustain production and sales through a demand downturn without any additional borrowing — 'we maintained production and sales to meet our expenses without any additional borrowing'
- Demonstrated technical capability to extend into new applications — first grinder delivered for a Medical Implements customer and a first Remanufacturing of a Cincinnati Grinder order received from an overseas customer
- Newly completed Halol plant fully ready with power and infrastructure, providing capacity headroom
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Single-segment, single-product concentration — Management states the Company is presently dealing in a single segment activity, namely Machine Tools – Centerless Grinding Machine. With no product or segment diversification, a downturn in demand for centreless grinders flows straight through to the whole business.
- Derived, cyclical demand from customer industries — The Machine Tool Industry is a supplementary industry: 'the growth opportunity for the machine tools industry is in direct proportion to the industrial growth of other industries like Textile Machinery Industry, Automobile Industry, Steel Industry, Bearing Industry'. Management further states that 'fortunes of company is directly linked to the growth and progress of the industry to which it caters', and the cautionary statement names cyclical demand and pricing in the Company's principal markets as a risk factor.
- Automobile end-market dependence — Growth has been driven by the automobile industry, and the stated opportunities rest on further automobile growth, multinational car manufacturers shifting production to India, and outsourcing of auto ancillary products. This concentrates the demand base on a single cyclical end-market.
- Trade policy and tariff shocks transmitted through customers — FY26 demonstrated the mechanism: 'The first two quarters were seriously affected by US Trade tariff issue. Though we did not get affected in direct sales, but majority of our domestic customers were affected seriously as their expansion plans were put on hold or cancelled.' The effect ran across three quarters. Import-export policies are also listed as a factor bearing on the industry.
- Execution risk in the Vadodara-to-Halol manufacturing shift — Manufacturing machines must be physically moved from Vadodara to the new Halol plant, a move already deferred once for cost and demand reasons. The shifting 'will start in next few weeks and would continue for next several months' — an extended period during which production continuity is at stake, notwithstanding management's assurance that production will not be affected.
- Internal control adequacy scaled only to current size — Controls are described as adequate only 'considering the size and nature of the business', with a review promised as the Company grows. Separately, the Board records that an 'Auditors Disclaimer report has been noted and additional financial control as required are being implemented' — an open control remediation.
- Regulatory / secretarial compliance gap pending before the NCLT — The secretarial auditor's observations concern a delay the Company attributes to inadvertence and oversight. The Company has initiated the procedure to file e-form INC-28 before the NCLT Mumbai bench (case no. CP (CAA) No. 277/MH-II/2019 connected with CA(CAA) No. 625/MH-II/2018) and is still 'in process of complying all the requirements of the Companies Act, 2013 and amended listing agreement'.
- Raw material availability and prices, and regulatory/macro change — The cautionary statement enumerates 'raw material availability and prices', 'changes in Government regulations, tax regimes, economic developments and Industrial growth within India and the countries in which the Company conducts business' as factors that could make actual results differ materially. Government policies and investment incentives for customer industries are likewise flagged as bearing on the industry.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

- Ability to sustain production and sales through a demand downturn without any additional borrowing — 'we maintained production and sales to meet our expenses without any additional borrowing'

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Complete the shift of manufacturing from Vadodara to the new Halol plant in a phased manner over several months so that production is not disrupted
- Extend the centreless grinder franchise into new application verticals — the first grinder for a Medical Implements customer was delivered, with more in the pipeline
- Build a remanufacturing line of business — a first-for-SMT order to remanufacture a Cincinnati Grinder was received from an overseas customer, with the machine to be shipped back in the next few months
- Sustain and widen the export market beyond the U.S.A. and Europe into Australia, South America and South East Asia
- Sustain growth through product innovation and cutting-edge technology, which management cites as the basis of the optimistic long-term industry outlook
- Use trade exhibitions as the route to market — participated in Engimach 2026 in Ahmedabad and will participate in IMTEX 2027 in Bangalore in January 2027
- Fund operations without additional borrowing, having maintained production and sales through the downturn to meet expenses without incremental debt
- Review and upgrade the internal control system as the Company achieves further growth and a higher level of operations
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company's principal expansion project is its new plant at Halol, Gujarat. The Halol plant work has been completed and all assets were capitalised in January 2026, with depreciation on the new added facility being provided from January 2026. The plant is now fully ready with power and all other infrastructure in place. The Company had deliberately delayed moving manufacturing machines from Vadodara to Halol for a few months in view of uncertainties in demand, to avoid the cost of moving and to prevent disruption to production; the shifting will start in the next few weeks and would continue for the next several months, ensuring that production does not get affected. Beyond the Halol project, additional assets were procured during the year and the Company invested in fixed deposits, mutual funds and carried bank balances to meet future needs. On the demand side, the Company delivered its first grinder for a Medical Implements customer with more in the pipeline, and received its first Remanufacturing of a Cincinnati Grinder order from an overseas customer.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Machine tool demand is directly proportional to industrial growth in the customer industries the Company supplies — textile machinery, automobile, steel and bearing industries
- Phenomenal growth in the automobile industry has largely driven machine tool demand, and further growth is anticipated as several multinational car manufacturers shift their production base to India
- Outsourcing of automobile ancillary products from India is cited as a further growth opportunity with tremendous potential in coming years
- The domestic auto production is growing rapidly to meet demand and to support newer models and technologies being developed
- Lower GST on vehicles and preferential GST for electric vehicles are described as a boon to the auto industry
- RBI is still predicting a 6.5% increase in GDP despite global turmoil
- Rising exports of engineering products and auto components support a better outlook
- Export markets to the U.S.A. and Europe will sustain, with an additional avenue opened for exports to Australia, South America and South East Asia; domestic demand will also grow in the current year
- FY26 was hurt by the US trade tariff issue: direct sales were not affected, but domestic customers put expansion plans on hold or cancelled them, affecting three quarters before conditions began changing around November
- The year 2026-2027 has started with substantial improvement over last year
- Long-term industry outlook is optimistic, based on product innovation and cutting-edge technology sustaining growth
- Government policies, import-export policies and investment incentives available to customer industries are stated as relevant factors bearing on the industry
- Currently, pending orders equivalent to about 5 months of production
- More grinders for the medical implements field are in the pipeline following the first delivery during the year
- A first Remanufacturing of Cincinnati Grinder order received from an overseas customer, with the machine to be shipped back to the customer in the next few months

risks.note: Management states the Company is presently dealing in a single segment activity, namely Machine Tools – Centerless Grinding Machine. With no product or segment diversification, a downturn in demand for centreless grinders flows straight through to the whole business.

risks.risk: Derived, cyclical demand from customer industries
risks.note: The Machine Tool Industry is a supplementary industry: 'the growth opportunity for the machine tools industry is in direct proportion to the industrial growth of other industries like Textile Machinery Industry, Automobile Industry, Steel Industry, Bearing Industry'. Management further states that 'fortunes of company is directly linked to the growth and progress of the industry to which it caters', and the cautionary statement names cyclical demand and pricing in the Company's principal markets as a risk factor.

Growth has been driven by the automobile industry, and the stated opportunities rest on further automobile growth, multinational car manufacturers shifting production to India, and outsourcing of auto ancillary products. This concentrates the demand base on a single cyclical end-market.

risks.risk: Trade policy and tariff shocks transmitted through customers
risks.note: FY26 demonstrated the mechanism: 'The first two quarters were seriously affected by US Trade tariff issue. Though we did not get affected in direct sales, but majority of our domestic customers were affected seriously as their expansion plans were put on hold or cancelled.' The effect ran across three quarters. Import-export policies are also listed as a factor bearing on the industry.

risks.risk: Execution risk in the Vadodara-to-Halol manufacturing shift
risks.note: Manufacturing machines must be physically moved from Vadodara to the new Halol plant, a move already deferred once for cost and demand reasons. The shifting 'will start in next few weeks and would continue for next several months' — an extended period during which production continuity is at stake, notwithstanding management's assurance that production will not be affected.

risks.risk: Internal control adequacy scaled only to current size
risks.note: Controls are described as adequate only 'considering the size and nature of the business', with a review promised as the Company grows. Separately, the Board records that an 'Auditors Disclaimer report has been noted and additional financial control as required are being implemented' — an open control remediation.

risks.risk: Regulatory / secretarial compliance gap pending before the NCLT
risks.note: The secretarial auditor's observations concern a delay the Company attributes to inadvertence and oversight. The Company has initiated the procedure to file e-form INC-28 before the NCLT Mumbai bench (case no. CP (CAA) No. 277/MH-II/2019 connected with CA(CAA) No. 625/MH-II/2018) and is still 'in process of complying all the requirements of the Companies Act, 2013 and amended listing agreement'.

risks.risk: Raw material availability and prices, and regulatory/macro change
risks.note: The cautionary statement enumerates 'raw material availability and prices', 'changes in Government regulations, tax regimes, economic developments and Industrial growth within India and the countries in which the Company conducts business' as factors that could make actual results differ materially. Government policies and investment incentives for customer industries are likewise flagged as bearing on the industry.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Machine tool demand is directly proportional to industrial growth in the customer industries the Company supplies — textile machinery, automobile, steel and bearing industries
- Phenomenal growth in the automobile industry has largely driven machine tool demand, and further growth is anticipated as several multinational car manufacturers shift their production base to India
- Outsourcing of automobile ancillary products from India is cited as a further growth opportunity with tremendous potential in coming years
- The domestic auto production is growing rapidly to meet demand and to support newer models and technologies being developed
- Lower GST on vehicles and preferential GST for electric vehicles are described as a boon to the auto industry
- RBI is still predicting a 6.5% increase in GDP despite global turmoil
- Rising exports of engineering products and auto components support a better outlook
- Export markets to the U.S.A. and Europe will sustain, with an additional avenue opened for exports to Australia, South America and South East Asia; domestic demand will also grow in the current year
- FY26 was hurt by the US trade tariff issue: direct sales were not affected, but domestic customers put expansion plans on hold or cancelled them, affecting three quarters before conditions began changing around November
- The year 2026-2027 has started with substantial improvement over last year
- Long-term industry outlook is optimistic, based on product innovation and cutting-edge technology sustaining growth
- Government policies, import-export policies and investment incentives available to customer industries are stated as relevant factors bearing on the industry
- Currently, pending orders equivalent to about 5 months of production
- More grinders for the medical implements field are in the pipeline following the first delivery during the year
- A first Remanufacturing of Cincinnati Grinder order received from an overseas customer, with the machine to be shipped back to the customer in the next few months

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Complete the shift of manufacturing from Vadodara to the new Halol plant in a phased manner over several months so that production is not disrupted
- Extend the centreless grinder franchise into new application verticals — the first grinder for a Medical Implements customer was delivered, with more in the pipeline
- Build a remanufacturing line of business — a first-for-SMT order to remanufacture a Cincinnati Grinder was received from an overseas customer, with the machine to be shipped back in the next few months
- Sustain and widen the export market beyond the U.S.A. and Europe into Australia, South America and South East Asia
- Sustain growth through product innovation and cutting-edge technology, which management cites as the basis of the optimistic long-term industry outlook
- Use trade exhibitions as the route to market — participated in Engimach 2026 in Ahmedabad and will participate in IMTEX 2027 in Bangalore in January 2027
- Fund operations without additional borrowing, having maintained production and sales through the downturn to meet expenses without incremental debt
- Review and upgrade the internal control system as the Company achieves further growth and a higher level of operations
